In detail

Historic Delfshaven — the harbour the Pilgrim Fathers sailed from — plus Spangen and Bospolder-Tussendijken behind it. Rotterdam runs a Veiligheidsindex as part of its Wijkprofiel, built from crime and nuisance figures together with a survey of around 30,000 residents between March and October 2025. Citywide it fell from 110 in 2022 to 104 in 2026, with the perception of safety dropping faster than the recorded figures. Tussendijken is among the five focus areas that improved against the city trend and beat the council's expectations. The historic harbour itself is calm and worth the trip; the surrounding streets are ordinary residential Rotterdam with a long-running improvement programme.

Frequently asked questions

Is Delfshaven safe?

Wandroz currently rates Delfshaven in Rotterdam as relatively safer than most other neighbourhoods in Rotterdam during the day and roughly average compared to other neighbourhoods in Rotterdam at night. This comes from a structured local-source assessment: an area-level review of credible local sources — local and national news, municipal and police-published material, and official surveys where they exist — consolidated across sources rather than taken from a single report. Rotterdam publishes no comparable neighbourhood-level crime dataset; where a city does, Wandroz uses it instead.

Is Delfshaven safe at night?

At night, Delfshaven is rated as roughly average compared to other neighbourhoods in Rotterdam. If you're unsure, it's worth checking recent local reviews for your specific street or block, since a neighbourhood-wide rating can't capture block-by-block variation.

Is Delfshaven a good area to stay in as a tourist?

Delfshaven's day rating (relatively safer than most other neighbourhoods in Rotterdam) is the more relevant one for typical daytime tourist activity; check the night rating too if you'll be out late.
